name: STITCH
question: Does continuous small-bites fascial closure reduce incisional hernia after elective midline laparotomy compared with conventional large-bites closure?

arms.label: Continuous small-bites fascial closure (5 mm bites and spacing, 2-0 polydioxanone on a 31 mm needle)
continuous large-bites fascial closure (1 cm bites and spacing, looped size 1 polydioxanone on a 48 mm needle)

design.population: 560 adults scheduled for elective abdominal surgery through a midline laparotomy at surgical and gynecological departments of ten Dutch hospitals.

verdictNote: Fewer hernias at 1 year with similar complications; bite size, suture gauge and needle size were changed together.
takeaway: Continuous small-bites fascial closure (5 mm bites, 2-0 polydioxanone) was compared with large-bites closure (1 cm bites, looped size 1 polydioxanone) in elective midline laparotomy: incisional hernia at 1 year was 13% versus 21% (adjusted OR 0.52), with similar complications and 4 minutes longer closure.

reports.label: 1-year randomized comparison
reports.citation: Deerenberg EB, Harlaar JJ, Steyerberg EW, et al. Small bites versus large bites for closure of abdominal midline incisions (STITCH): a double-blind, multicentre, randomised controlled trial. *Lancet.* 2015;386(10000):1254-1260.
reports.followUp: 1-year visit, defined as a visit up to month 15 after surgery; follow-up ended Aug 30, 2013

results.measure: Incisional hernia at the 1-year visit (clinical examination, ultrasonography or CT; EHS definition), 545 of 560 analyzed
results.note: Covariate-adjusted odds ratio; unadjusted chi-squared p=0.0220. Sample size was set to detect 15% versus 7.5% with 80% power (259 per group); the protocol's Cox analysis was replaced by a binary endpoint at up to 15 months.

results.measure: Mean time of fascial closure, minutes (SD)
results.note: Mean difference derived from the two reported means; the Discussion states a mean additional closure time of 4 min.

results.measure: Mean length of hospital stay, days (SD)
First-week visual analogue pain scores; SF-36 and EQ-5D at 12 months (452 of 483 patients completed the questionnaires)
results.note: The report states that pain scores and SF-36 and EQ-5D results did not differ significantly between groups; the data are not shown. Patients who developed incisional hernia had lower SF-36 general health scores than those without (mean 60.16 versus 64.84; p=0.0326).

harms.label: Surgical site infection
harms.note: p=0.419. Superficial incisional 23/276 (8%) versus 33/284 (12%); deep incisional 8/276 (3%) versus 12/284 (4%); organ or space 27/276 (10%) versus 23/284 (8%).

harms.label: Relaparotomy within 1 year
harms.note: Counts taken from the trial profile; no between-group test is reported.

harms.label: Death within 1 year
harms.note: Counts taken from the trial profile; no between-group test is reported.

delivery.label: Small-bites technique
delivery.value: At least twice as many stitches as the incision length in cm, with USP 2-0 PDS Plus II on a 31 mm needle, tissue bites of 5 mm and intersuture spacing of 5 mm; each stitch took aponeurosis only, avoiding fat and muscle.

delivery.label: Large-bites technique
delivery.value: Mass closure with tissue bites of at least 1 cm and intersuture spacing of 1 cm, using USP 1 double-loop PDS Plus II on a 48 mm needle.

delivery.label: Closure sequence
delivery.value: In both groups suturing began at both ends of the incision toward the centre, with at least 2 cm of overlap between the cranial and caudal sutures, which were knotted separately; an additional knot from each was allowed. Both techniques aimed for a suture length to wound length ratio of 4:1 or higher.

delivery.label: Timing of randomization
delivery.value: About 15 min before closure, during surgery; stratified by centre and by surgeon versus resident with minimization.

delivery.label: Ratio of suture length to wound length
delivery.note: p<0.0001. Total suture used 110 (SD 39) versus 95 (SD 34) cm; mean wound length 22 (SD 5) cm in both groups.

delivery.label: Allocated intervention not received
delivery.note: Both small-bites patients who did not receive the allocated closure had fragile fascia.

values.exp: Lower GI 140 (51%); upper GI 74 (27%); gynecological 41 (15%); vascular 21 (8%)
values.ctl: Lower GI 133 (47%); upper GI 89 (31%); gynecological 41 (14%); vascular 21 (7%)

delivery.label: Methods of follow-up assessment (545 patients)
delivery.value: Clinical and radiological examination in 338 (62%), radiological examination alone in 76 (14%) and physical examination alone in 131 (24%); radiological findings were decisive when observations conflicted.

delivery.label: Detection of hernia in 87 patients with hernia assessed by both methods
delivery.value: Found by both in 43 (49%), by imaging alone in 41 (47%) and by physical examination alone in 3 (3%).

reports.label: 13-year follow-up
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed issue date (June 2026); the online date was not confirmed
reports.citation: van den Berg R, van Egmond S, Smits F, et al. Small bites vs large bites for closure of abdominal midline incisions: a randomized clinical trial. *JAMA Surg.* 2026;161(6):566-573.
reports.followUp: median time to censoring 8 years (IQR 2-13), 13 years after accrual ended

results.measure: Cumulative incidence of incisional hernia (clinical and radiologic) at 13 years, time-to-event analysis accounting for competing risks
results.note: 275 patients in the small-bites group and 284 in the control group.

results.measure: Cumulative incidence of incisional hernia wider than 20 mm at 13 years
Mean hernia width at final follow-up

results.note: The abstract reports the repair rates as similar and gives no counts.

delivery.label: Imaging at final follow-up
delivery.value: 170 patients were alive without evidence of incisional hernia at final follow-up, and 122 of them (72%) had additional abdominal ultrasound; imaging done as part of patient care was available for 238 patients.
